newsitem.title: UK: LME copper knocked below $2,000 in late activity.
newsitem.headline: LME copper knocked below $2,000 in late activity.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) 3-months copper prices dropped below $2,000 per tonne in post-kerb inter-office activity on Friday.

Copper last traded on the kerb at $2,007 -- down $10 from Thursday and compared with a Friday high of $2,028. Late bouts of profit taking had knocked the market from the high. Later, in thin volume and after what technical analysts regarded as a less than constructive kerb close, traders said it was hit by a big sell order. That drew in selling from New York to take it down through support at $2,000 to the more robust area at $1,985 where it seemed to be holding by around 1800GMT.
A burst of investment bank buying and shortcovering had pushed copper higher toward the end of the week.
Aluminium also firmed during the week on tight supply for January and speculative interest but it eased on Friday under disappointed liquidation after failing to build on earlier gains up to $1,468.
Freer lending of the spreads helped to dent upside sentiment. It was assessed just below $1,450 by 1800 GMT.
